findings.issue_text: [BUG] The Google Meet fallback dereferences mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration without optional chaining after `evt.destinationCalendar ?? []`, so a null or empty destinationCalendar produces undefined.integration (TypeError), whereas the pre-diff code used `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`. Every booking created with a Google Meet location and no destination calendar — exactly the 'Meet selected without a Google Cal' scenario this fallback exists to handle, and the case handleNewBooking now encodes as `destinationCalendar: null` — throws inside EventManager.create and the booking request fails with a 500 instead of falling back to Cal Video.

[BUG] The slug spread condition is inverted: `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})` replaces the original `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })`, while the paired requestedSlug line keeps its original billing-enabled gating, so the two conditions no longer form the intended either/or. On billing-disabled (self-hosted) deployments organizations are now created with neither slug nor requestedSlug (previously slug), leaving the org without a working URL; on billing-enabled deployments the slug is assigned at creation time (previously only metadata.requestedSlug until payment), bypassing the team-billing gate.

[BUG] For COLLECTIVE events where neither eventType.destinationCalendar nor organizerUser.destinationCalendar exists, evt.destinationCalendar is set to null, so `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is skipped and the team members' destination calendars already collected in teamDestinationCalendars are silently discarded. The PR's core scenario — creating the event on every collective host's chosen calendar — no-ops whenever the organizer has no destination calendar: member events fall back to credential defaults instead of their selected calendars, with no error or log to indicate the drop.

[BUG] In updateEvent the fallback branch evaluates `find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` with a falsy externalCalendarId, comparing every calendar's externalId against undefined/null so it always returns undefined, making the previous `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` fallback dead code. For booking references without externalCalendarId (legacy references and the no-credentialId destination path), calendar.events.update is called with calendarId undefined and the remote event is never updated on reschedule, leaving stale event times on calendars.

[BUG] deleteEvent has the same dead fallback: with a falsy externalCalendarId, `find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` can never match a DestinationCalendar row (externalId is a required column), so calendarId resolves to undefined instead of the destination calendar's externalId. Cancellations of bookings whose reference lacks externalCalendarId (e.g., old references created before externalCalendarId was persisted) now delete from 'primary' and 404 instead of deleting from the calendar the event lives on, leaving ghost calendar events behind.

[BUG] createEvent selects the target calendar solely via `find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)`, which can never match when the destination has no credentialId (the EventManager else-branch passes credentials whose ids differ from the null destination.credentialId), so selectedCalendar is undefined and the event is inserted into 'primary'. For DestinationCalendar rows with null credentialId, events land on the user's primary calendar instead of the chosen destination calendar (pre-diff code inserted into destinationCalendar.externalId), while the stored reference still points at the destination's externalId, so later updates/deletes target a calendar that never held the event.

[BUG] The newBookingId merge path still deletes only the first old calendar reference via `booking.references.find(...)`, left unchanged while this PR makes collective bookings carry one calendar reference per host. Rescheduling or merging a collective booking deletes the old calendar event of the first host only, leaving orphaned calendar events on the remaining hosts' calendars.

[ADVISORY] Per-destination targeting is implemented only in GoogleCalendarService; BaseCalendarService (Apple/CalDav and its subclasses), Lark and Office365 still resolve the target from destinationCalendar[0] and ignore the per-destination credentialId/externalId that the new createAllCalendarEvents loop passes. For collective multi-host bookings on non-Google providers, iterations beyond the first host request destination[0]'s calendar with a different host's credentials — CalDav's filter matches none of its calendars (silent no-op) and Lark/O365 get an API error that CalendarManager swallows — so the other hosts' calendar events are silently never created.

[ADVISORY] The reference builder changed non-calendar results from `credentialId: result.credentialId` to `credentialId: undefined`, so video booking references stop persisting the id of the credential that created the meeting. Booking references for video apps lose the credential linkage they have carried until now; consumers that match booking references by credentialId (e.g., credential-removal cleanup flows) silently stop finding video bookings created after this change.

[ADVISORY] The recurring-cancellation sweep, which deletes every remaining booking's event across all calendar credentials, now runs once per calendar reference inside the new for-loop instead of once per booking. Cancelling all remaining bookings of a recurring collective booking with N calendar references fires the identical deletion sweep N times, doubling calendar API calls and logging errors for the duplicate (already-deleted) events.

[BUG] The Google Meet fallback dereferences mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration without a guard, so evt.destinationCalendar being null or an empty array throws TypeError, where the replaced optional-chained check gracefully fell back to Cal Video. Any booking scheduled with location integrations:google:meet and no destination calendar crashes with TypeError: the Stripe/PayPal success webhooks now build destinationCalendar: [] for organizers without a calendar (webhook.ts:229) and then call EventManager.create, so the payment is captured but the booking is never scheduled and the webhook returns 500.

[BUG] The slug spread condition was inverted: `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` became `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`, so slug is now written when team billing is enabled instead of disabled, while requestedSlug keeps its original enabled-only condition. With IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED=false, organizations are created with neither slug nor requestedSlug and have no working URL; with the flag true, the slug is claimed immediately at creation, bypassing the requestedSlug-then-upgrade flow the metadata field exists to defer.

[BUG] Only evt.destinationCalendar[0] is connected to the booking (the Booking.destinationCalendar relation stays one-to-one), so the collected team destination calendars exist only in the in-memory evt and are lost on persistence. Flows that rebuild evt from the booking afterwards — booking confirmation (confirm.handler.ts:175) and payment success (webhook.ts:229, paypal-webhook.ts:152) — construct destinationCalendar with only the main host's calendar, so paid or confirmation-gated COLLECTIVE bookings get their calendar event created only in the main host's calendar and the other hosts' calendars never receive the event.

[BUG] updateEvent's fallback `find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` executes only when externalCalendarId is already falsy and then compares externalId against that same falsy value, so it can never match and always yields undefined. For booking references without externalCalendarId (produced by the credentialId-less destination path, which now persists externalCalendarId: result.externalId = undefined), rescheduling passes calendarId undefined to calendar.events.update and the update fails, where the previous code fell back to the booking's destination calendar.

[BUG] deleteEvent has the same dead fallback: `find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` runs only when externalCalendarId is falsy and compares against that falsy value, so it never matches and the intended destination-calendar fallback is unreachable. Cancellation of a booking whose reference lacks externalCalendarId resolves calendarId to undefined (falling back to 'primary') instead of the calendar the event was created in, leaving the original calendar event orphaned and its slot busy.

[BUG] createEvent still targets destinationCalendar[0] regardless of which credential invokes it; the per-credential calendar selection implemented for Google was not carried over to Office365. For a COLLECTIVE booking with multiple Office365 hosts, every per-host createEvent call writes to (or fails with 401/404 against) the first host's calendar, so the other hosts' calendars never receive the event — the PR's core requirement is unimplemented for Office365.

[BUG] Lark's createEvent (and identically createAttendees, updateEvent and deleteEvent) resolves the calendar from destinationCalendar[0] instead of the destination matching the executing credential, so the per-credential selection was not carried over. For a COLLECTIVE booking with multiple Lark hosts, every per-host createEvent call targets the first host's calendar, so the other hosts' calendars never receive the event and the first host's calendar can receive duplicates.

[BUG] BaseCalendarService (Apple/CalDav) filters calendars against destinationCalendar[0]'s externalId regardless of which credential invokes it, so the per-credential selection implemented for Google was not carried over. For a COLLECTIVE booking with multiple CalDav/Apple hosts, each per-host createEvent call pins to the first host's calendar — hosts without access to it silently create nothing and the other hosts' calendars never receive the event.

[BUG] The recurring-cancellation loop still reads only the first calendar reference per booking with references.find, while this same diff converted the non-recurring path to references.filter over all references. Cancelling all remaining bookings of a recurring COLLECTIVE event deletes only the first host's calendar events; the other hosts' recurring events stay on their calendars and keep the slots busy.

[BUG] The newBookingId merge path still picks oldCalendarEvent with references.find while calendarReference in the same function was converted to a filter over all references. Rescheduling a multi-host collective booking into an existing booking deletes only the first host's old calendar event; the other hosts' old events are orphaned and keep the old slot busy.

[BUG] evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars) is a silent no-op when neither eventType nor organizerUser has a destination calendar (evt.destinationCalendar is null), discarding the collected team calendars. A COLLECTIVE event whose organizer has no calendar app installed creates no calendar events at all even though the other hosts have destination calendars — the exact scenario the PR targets.

[BUG] Team destination calendars are collected only under isTeamEventType && schedulingType === 'COLLECTIVE', which excludes dynamic collective bookings (multiple users via dynamicUserList carry no schedulingType), and the removed comment explicitly listed 'dynamic collective events' as part of the requirement. Dynamic group bookings (user1+user2) still create the calendar event only for the first user; that half of the requirement is silently dropped by this PR.

[BUG] The only test-shaped change in the diff updates an expected webhook payload field (null to []); no test in the diff exercises the multi-host collective path — teamDestinationCalendars collection, the per-destination loop in createAllCalendarEvents, Google's per-credential calendar matching, or the credential-from-DB fallbacks. Regressions in the PR's core behavior — the first-calendar-only behavior remaining in Office365/Lark/BaseCalendarService, or the EventManager TypeError on empty destinationCalendar — ship undetected.

[ADVISORY] Each per-host createEvent call performs its own insert with conferenceDataVersion: 1, so a COLLECTIVE booking using Google Meet generates one conference per host calendar instead of one shared link. Hosts 2..N get calendar events whose Meet link differs from the link attendees receive (the booking stores the first result), so participants join different meetings.

[ADVISORY] The 'fetch credential from DB' block is copy-pasted three times (createAllCalendarEvents, updateAllCalendarEvents, handleCancelBooking) and has already drifted: the EventManager copies map appName from app.slug while the handleCancelBooking copy fetches the bare credential with no app include. The next change to credential resolution must be applied in three places and will silently miss one, as the existing drift between the copies already demonstrates.

[ADVISORY] createAllCalendarEvents awaits createEvent sequentially per destination (for...of plus await), where the previous single-calendar path and the credentialId-less branch use Promise.all. COLLECTIVE booking latency grows by one full calendar-API round trip per host on the synchronous booking-creation request path (e.g. five Google hosts add five sequential API calls before the booking responds).

[BUG] The Google Meet fallback dereferences `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` with no guard, so a null or empty destinationCalendar throws instead of falling back to Cal Video as the pre-diff optional chain did. Any booking with a Google Meet location and no destination calendar — evt.destinationCalendar is null via handleNewBooking's `: null` branch, or [] from the payment-webhook/confirm/editLocation handlers — throws TypeError inside EventManager.create, turning booking creation/approval into a 500 for exactly the 'Meet selected w/o a Google Cal' scenario this check exists to handle.

[BUG] The slug spread condition is inverted: `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` was rewritten to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`, setting slug exactly when it previously was not set (the metadata/requestedSlug line kept its original polarity). With team billing enabled, organizations are created with a slug immediately, bypassing the requestedSlug-in-metadata pending flow the adjacent line still implements; with it disabled, organizations are created with no slug at all, breaking /org/{slug} routing for every new organization. This file is untouched by the destinationCalendar intent — pure untraceable drift that flips production behavior.

[BUG] updateEvent's fallback was changed to `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`, which compares each calendar's externalId against the very externalCalendarId that is absent in that branch, so the fallback always evaluates to undefined. Updating a booking whose calendar reference carries no externalCalendarId now calls events.update with calendarId undefined and fails, leaving the existing calendar event with stale times after reschedule.

[BUG] deleteEvent has the same self-referential fallback (`find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` in the branch where externalCalendarId is falsy), always yielding undefined calendarId. Cancelling a booking whose reference lacks externalCalendarId fails to delete the calendar event, orphaning it on the host's calendar.

[BUG] Office365CalendarService.createEvent ignores which credential is creating the event and always targets destinationCalendar[0], while EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents now calls createEvent once per destination. For a collective booking with more than one O365 host, only the first host's calendar receives the event; every other host's call posts to `/me/calendars/{firstHostCalendarId}/events` under their own auth, 404s, and is swallowed by CalendarManager's catch — the other hosts' calendars silently never get the event, so the PR's stated collective multi-host goal only works for Google Calendar.

[BUG] LarkCalendarService (createEvent, createAttendees, updateEvent, deleteEvent) all resolve the calendar from destinationCalendar[0] regardless of which credential is acting, so per-destination calls from EventManager all hit the first host's calendar. Collective bookings with multiple Lark hosts create the event only in the first host's calendar; the remaining hosts' create calls target a foreign calendarId and fail, and CalendarManager swallows the error — silently missing events for all non-first hosts.

[BUG] BaseCalendarService filters the credential owner's own calendar list by destinationCalendar[0].externalId, which never matches when the acting credential belongs to a different host of a collective booking. For multi-host collectives on CalDav/ICS-backed services, the other hosts' create calls produce an empty filtered list and silently create nothing — only the first host's calendar gets the event.

[BUG] `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is a no-op when the base assignment produced null (neither eventType.destinationCalendar nor organizerUser.destinationCalendar exists), discarding every collected team calendar. A collective booking whose organizer has no calendar connected but whose team members do keeps evt.destinationCalendar null, so EventManager takes the create-in-organizer-credentials fallback and the members' calendars get nothing — the multi-host feature silently does nothing for exactly the mixed-configuration teams it targets.

[BUG] The approval path rebuilds evt.destinationCalendar from the single booking.destinationCalendar — and handleNewBooking only ever connects destinationCalendar[0] to the booking — so requires-confirmation collective bookings can never create per-host calendar events. Approving a COLLECTIVE booking with requiresConfirmation creates the calendar event in the main host's calendar only; the other hosts' calendars never receive it, and the per-host data needed at approval time was never persisted, so this path is structurally outside the PR's stated intent.

[BUG] The recurring-cancellation branch still selects a single reference with `updBooking.references.find((ref) => ref.type.includes("_calendar"))` and is now re-executed once per calendar reference by the new outer loop. Cancelling all remaining bookings of a recurring COLLECTIVE event deletes only the first host's calendar events per booking (the other hosts' events survive on their calendars) while issuing duplicate delete calls for the main host's events — the multi-reference world this PR creates is not handled here.

[ADVISORY] Team-calendar collection skips users[0] on the assumption that the organizer is always the first loaded user, while the base calendar comes from organizerUser — nothing in the diff enforces users[0] === organizerUser. If the event-type owner is not first in hosts, one host's calendar is never added (skipped by slice(1), absent from the base) and the organizer's calendar is added twice — two destinations sharing one credentialId make Google createEvent run twice against the same calendar, producing duplicate events.

[ADVISORY] loadUsers is wholesale rewritten (try/catch error mapping, hosts-fallback restructure, dropped `organization: { select: { slug: true } }`) with no connection to the destinationCalendar change. Dynamic-username bookings no longer load user.organization, so any org-scoped consumer downstream now sees undefined, and Prisma failures during user load are remapped to a 400 carrying the raw Prisma message or a generic 500 — unrelated behavior changes riding inside a calendar PR.

[ADVISORY] `schedulingType?: SchedulingType | null` is added to the shared CalendarEvent contract and populated on every booking in handleNewBooking, but nothing in this diff ever reads it. Ships-inert surface on the core event type: every future CalendarEvent producer must decide what to populate there, and readers may assume it is meaningful when no consumer defines its contract.

[ADVISORY] The catch block in updateAllCalendarEvents deleted its only logging (`console.error(message)`) while expanding to per-reference failure results, so failures are returned but never recorded. Reschedule calendar-update failures now surface as silent failure entries with no server-side trace, leaving operators unable to diagnose why calendars stopped syncing.

[ADVISORY] The fetch-credential-from-DB-and-map-to-CredentialWithAppName block is hand-duplicated in createAllCalendarEvents and updateAllCalendarEvents, with a third already-diverging copy in handleCancelBooking (its prisma.credential.findUnique omits the app include). Three places must be updated in lockstep for any credential-shape change and they have already drifted; the create-path copy also runs one sequential prisma.credential.findUnique per destination inside the booking hot path, an N+1 that grows with collective size.

[ADVISORY] The no-credentialId destination branch calls `createEvent(c, event)` without the new externalId argument, so EventResult.externalId is undefined and the booking reference loses the externalCalendarId the old `evt.destinationCalendar?.externalId` code stored. Bookings created through that legacy path persist references without externalCalendarId, which later route update/delete into the broken Google fallback (undefined calendarId) instead of the intended calendar.

[ADVISORY] The only test change in the diff is the webhook payload expectation (`destinationCalendar: []`); none of the new behavior — the per-destination creation loop, Google's credentialId matching, or the collective calendar collection in handleNewBooking — is exercised by any test. A regression in the multi-host creation path (the null-push discard, the users[0] ordering assumption, or the credentialId mismatch fallback to 'primary') ships undetected and surfaces as bookings with missing or duplicated calendar events.

[BUG] The Google Meet fallback reads mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration without optional chaining after destructuring `evt.destinationCalendar ?? []`, so a null or empty destinationCalendar yields undefined and the property access throws a TypeError. Every booking with location integrations:google:meet whose eventType/organizer has no destination calendar — exactly the 'Meet selected without a Google Cal' case this branch exists to handle — crashes inside EventManager.create, turning a previously-working fallback-to-Cal-Video booking into a 500.

[BUG] The slug spread condition is inverted by this diff: the old code wrote slug when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is false (`...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })`), the new ternary writes it only when it is true, while the adjacent requestedSlug line keeps the original semantics. On deployments where IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is false (self-hosted default), organization creation no longer persists slug, so newly created organizations have no URL identifier and are broken until manually fixed; on billing-enabled deployments slug is now written pre-payment, changing the paid-onboarding gating. This drive-by change is also unrelated to the destinationCalendar purpose of the PR.

[BUG] updateEvent's fallback branch evaluates `find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` only when externalCalendarId is falsy, so the predicate compares every calendar's externalId against undefined, never matches, and selectedCalendar resolves to undefined instead of the previous `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`. Updates/reschedules of bookings whose calendar reference lacks externalCalendarId (legacy references, or references created by the no-credentialId create path where result.externalId is undefined) now pass calendarId: undefined to calendar.events.update — the call fails instead of targeting the destination calendar, so the Google event keeps the old slot while the booking is rescheduled.

[BUG] deleteEvent's fallback has the same always-false predicate: in the branch where externalCalendarId is falsy, `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` can never be true, so calendarId resolves to undefined instead of the destination calendar's externalId. Cancelling such bookings deletes from the wrong calendar (the 'primary' defaultCalendarId defined immediately above) or errors out, leaving the original event in the real destination calendar as a ghost busy slot.

[BUG] Office365CalendarService.createEvent is left on the old single-argument signature and resolves the target as destinationCalendar[0] (mainHostDestinationCalendar), ignoring both the new credentialId parameter and which destination the caller is creating for — the credential-aware find exists only in GoogleCalendarService. For collective bookings with multiple destination calendars, EventManager's per-host loop calls O365 createEvent once per host credential, but every call targets host 1's calendar: host N's event is created in host 1's calendar (duplicate) or fails with 401/404, and host N's own calendar never receives the event.

[BUG] BaseCalendarService.createEvent (parent of the CalDav/Apple services) still filters calendars against destinationCalendar[0] and ignores the new credentialId argument, so the credential-aware target selection introduced for Google is absent for every provider built on this base class. Collective bookings with multiple CalDav/Apple destination calendars create every per-host event in the first host's calendar (or fail per credential), so non-primary hosts' calendars never receive the event — the exact multi-host scenario this PR claims to fix silently does not work outside Google.

[BUG] LarkCalendarService.createEvent is left on the old single-argument signature and always targets destinationCalendar[0] via mainHostDestinationCalendar, ignoring the credentialId the manager now passes. For collective bookings with multiple Lark destination calendars, each per-host createEvent call writes to the first host's calendar (or fails with a permission error), so non-primary hosts' Lark calendars never receive the event.

[BUG] evt.destinationCalendar is null when neither eventType.destinationCalendar nor organizerUser.destinationCalendar exists, and the teammates' calendars are appended via `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`, which is a silent no-op on null. A COLLECTIVE booking where the organizer has no connected calendar but teammates do silently drops every teammate's destination calendar — no calendar events are created for anyone despite hosts having calendars, defeating the feature for exactly the multi-host case it was written for.

[BUG] The BOOKING_REJECTED webhook payload's destinationCalendar field changes shape from DestinationCalendar|null to DestinationCalendar[] (null becomes []) — an unversioned breaking change to the public webhook contract, evidenced by the updated assertion `destinationCalendar: []`. Existing webhook consumers (Zapier/Make/custom endpoints) reading payload.destinationCalendar.externalId silently get undefined on every booking payload, breaking downstream calendar syncs with no error signal and no payload version bump.

[ADVISORY] createEvent receives destination.externalId but forwards only credential.id to calendar.createEvent, forcing every service to re-derive its target calendar (Google via a credentialId scan, the others incorrectly via [0]) even though the resolved externalId was already in hand at the call site. The target-calendar policy is duplicated per service instead of resolved once by the manager; forwarding externalId (which is already threaded into the result) would let Lark/O365/Base delete their broken [0] fallbacks and make the new credentialId parameter unnecessary — the next provider added to the app store will repeat the same mistake.

[ADVISORY] The ~25-line 'fetch credential from DB and reshape into CredentialWithAppName' block is copy-pasted three times (EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents here, EventManager.updateAllCalendarEvents ~510-535, handleCancelBooking ~428-438) and the copies already drift — the handleCancelBooking copy omits the app include and assigns the raw Prisma Credential. The next change to credential shaping (e.g., handling credentials whose app relation is missing, which the `app?.slug` gate currently silently drops, skipping the calendar with no error) must be replicated in three places and will inevitably miss one, producing inconsistent create/update/cancel behavior for the same credential.

[ADVISORY] The diff replaces the SchedulingType.COLLECTIVE / SchedulingType.ROUND_ROBIN enum comparisons with bare string literals ("COLLECTIVE", "ROUND_ROBIN"), repeated at three sites (~689, ~988, ~1077) instead of a named typed constant. A typo or enum-value rename no longer fails compilation — a misspelled literal in the includes() array silently evaluates false, flipping isTeamEventType and the collective destination-calendar behavior with none of the compile-check protection the previous enum constants provided.

[ADVISORY] The recurring-event deletion branch now executes once per calendar reference inside the new for-loop, so for a collective recurring booking the full credentials×remainingBookings delete fan-out runs once per host reference instead of once. Cancelling a collective recurring booking with H hosts issues H×M×K delete calls (M calendar credentials × K remaining bookings) where (H−1)×M×K are redundant re-deletes of already-deleted events, exposing cancellation to calendar API rate limits and flooding logs with 404/410 errors.

[ADVISORY] createAllCalendarEvents now awaits each destination's calendar creation (plus a possible per-destination credential DB fetch) sequentially in a for-loop, while the sibling no-credentialId branch still uses Promise.all. Booking-creation latency for collective events grows linearly with host count — a 5-host collective serializes 5 calendar API calls plus any DB fetches on the hot booking path, adding multiple seconds that parallel creation (as the adjacent branch already does) would avoid.

[BUG] This unrelated handler inverts the billing flag condition: the old code set the organization slug only when team billing was disabled (`...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })`), the new code sets it only when enabled (`...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`), while the requestedSlug line on the next line keeps the original `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` condition — a silent objective change smuggled into a destinationCalendar PR. On deployments where IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is false (e.g., self-hosting without Stripe), newly created organizations stop getting their slug written at creation, breaking org URL/slug reservation until manually repaired; on billing-enabled deployments the slug is now written immediately, changing the paid signup flow — neither change is part of the accepted PR objective.

[BUG] The Google Meet fallback drops the optional chaining the old code had: `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` is evaluated on the `undefined` element destructured from `evt.destinationCalendar ?? []`, so when destinationCalendar is null or empty the line throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'integration')` instead of falling back. Any booking flow with location 'integrations:google:meet' and no destination calendar — exactly the 'Meet selected w/o a Google Cal' case this branch exists for, and reachable because handleNewBooking sets destinationCalendar to null and confirm/editLocation handlers now set it to [] — crashes with a 500 instead of downgrading to Cal Video.

[BUG] updateEvent's no-externalCalendarId fallback now searches for a calendar whose externalId equals the falsy `externalCalendarId` it is falling back from (`find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)`), so `selectedCalendar` is always undefined and the update is sent with `calendarId: undefined`. Updates of Google Calendar events whose booking reference lacks externalCalendarId (references produced by the no-credentialId multi-credential path in createAllCalendarEvents, which calls createEvent without an externalId, 'other_calendar' references passing `?? null`, and legacy rows) now fail against the Google API instead of updating the destination calendar, leaving stale events that keep blocking slots.

[BUG] deleteEvent has the same self-comparison fallback (`find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` evaluated only when externalCalendarId is falsy), so `calendarId` resolves to undefined and the delete call fails. Cancellations of Google Calendar events without an externalCalendarId on the booking reference no longer delete the event — orphaned events remain on hosts' calendars and Google returns an error for the undefined calendar id, where the pre-refactor code used `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`.

[BUG] evt.destinationCalendar is null when neither eventType.destinationCalendar nor organizerUser.destinationCalendar exists, and the collective push `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is a no-op on null, so the team members' destination calendars collected in teamDestinationCalendars are silently discarded. For a COLLECTIVE event type whose organizer has no calendar connected but whose members do, no calendar events are created for anyone — the PR's multi-host objective silently does nothing for exactly the configuration it was written to handle.

[BUG] Office365 createEvent still resolves its target calendar from `destinationCalendar[0]` (the main host's calendar) instead of the destination entry matching the credential creating the event, so for collective bookings it builds `/me/calendars/<main-host-externalId>/events` with a calendar id foreign to the authenticating account. In a collective booking where hosts use different calendar accounts or providers (e.g., organizer on Google, member on Office365), the member's event creation calls the O365 API with the organizer's calendar id, fails, and is swallowed by CalendarManager's catch — the member's calendar silently gets no event.

[BUG] Lark createEvent (and identically createAttendees, updateEvent, deleteEvent in this file) resolves calendarId from `destinationCalendar[0]`, the main host's calendar, rather than from the destination belonging to the credential performing the call. For collective bookings with more than one host, every non-first host's Lark credential receives the main host's calendar externalId, so those create/update/delete calls target a wrong or nonexistent calendar and the extra hosts' calendar events silently fail.

[BUG] BaseCalendarService.createEvent filters the creating credential's own calendars by `mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId` (destinationCalendar[0], the first host's calendar), which matches nothing on any other host's CalDav account. For collective bookings on CalDav/Fastmail-style providers with more than one host, the second and later hosts' createEvent calls filter to an empty calendar list and silently create no event, so only the first host's calendar receives the booking despite the multi-host intent.

[BUG] The new per-reference loop re-runs the recurring-event branch once per calendar reference, but that branch still uses `updBooking.references.find((ref) => ref.type.includes("_calendar"))` (first match only), so with N references the first reference's events are deleted N times and references 2..N are never deleted. Cancelling all remaining bookings of a recurring COLLECTIVE booking leaves every non-primary host's calendar events on their calendars (orphaned busy slots) while issuing duplicate delete API calls for the primary host's events.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Office365CalendarService.createEvent is left on the old single-argument signature and resolves the target as destinationCalendar[0] (mainHostDestinationCalendar), ignoring both the new credentialId parameter and which destination the caller is creating for — the credential-aware find exists only in GoogleCalendarService. For collective bookings with multiple destination calendars, EventManager's per-host loop calls O365 createEvent once per host credential, but every call targets host 1's calendar: host N's event is created in host 1's calendar (duplicate) or fails with 401/404, and host N's own calendar never receives the event.

[BUG] BaseCalendarService.createEvent (parent of the CalDav/Apple services) still filters calendars against destinationCalendar[0] and ignores the new credentialId argument, so the credential-aware target selection introduced for Google is absent for every provider built on this base class. Collective bookings with multiple CalDav/Apple destination calendars create every per-host event in the first host's calendar (or fail per credential), so non-primary hosts' calendars never receive the event — the exact multi-host scenario this PR claims to fix silently does not work outside Google.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the Calendar interface to `createEvent(event: CalendarEvent, credentialId: number)` and CalendarManager now calls `calendar.createEvent(calEvent, credential.id)` for all providers. However, `BaseCalendarService` (used by CalDav/Apple-derived services) still selects the target calendar solely by destructuring the first element of `event.destinationCalendar` (`const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []`) and filtering calendars by that single `externalId`. There is no credentialId-based selection analogous to the new Google logic (`find(cal => cal.credentialId === credentialId)`). With `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` now passing an event whose `destinationCalendar` may contain multiple hosts' destinations, this base implementation will either (a) always target the first host's calendar, or (b) filter out all calendars for other credentials (if their calendar list doesn't contain the first host's externalId), causing missing events for non-primary hosts. This directly matches the finding and is a correctness defect exposed by the refactor.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] LarkCalendarService.createEvent is left on the old single-argument signature and always targets destinationCalendar[0] via mainHostDestinationCalendar, ignoring the credentialId the manager now passes. For collective bookings with multiple Lark destination calendars, each per-host createEvent call writes to the first host's calendar (or fails with a permission error), so non-primary hosts' Lark calendars never receive the event.
matched_golden_ids: The Calendar interface now requires createEvent(event, credentialId), but some implementations (e.g., Lark/Office365) still declare createEvent(event) only—this breaks the interface contract (also applies to other locations in the PR).
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that LarkCalendarService.createEvent still uses the old single-argument signature and ignores the new credentialId passed by the manager, which is exactly the interface-contract break described in the golden comment (and it even elaborates on the resulting behavioral bug).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] evt.destinationCalendar is null when neither eventType.destinationCalendar nor organizerUser.destinationCalendar exists, and the teammates' calendars are appended via `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`, which is a silent no-op on null. A COLLECTIVE booking where the organizer has no connected calendar but teammates do silently drops every teammate's destination calendar — no calendar events are created for anyone despite hosts having calendars, defeating the feature for exactly the multi-host case it was written for.

adjudication.rationale: In `handleNewBooking.ts`, `evt.destinationCalendar` is set to `null` when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` exists (`destinationCalendar: ... : null`). Immediately after, for COLLECTIVE team events, teammates' destination calendars are added via `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`, which is a silent no-op when `destinationCalendar` is `null`. This drops all teammate calendars in exactly the case described (organizer has none, teammates do), preventing the new multi-destination behavior from being applied.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The BOOKING_REJECTED webhook payload's destinationCalendar field changes shape from DestinationCalendar|null to DestinationCalendar[] (null becomes []) — an unversioned breaking change to the public webhook contract, evidenced by the updated assertion `destinationCalendar: []`. Existing webhook consumers (Zapier/Make/custom endpoints) reading payload.destinationCalendar.externalId silently get undefined on every booking payload, breaking downstream calendar syncs with no error signal and no payload version bump.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly changes `destinationCalendar` from a single `DestinationCalendar | null` to `DestinationCalendar[] | null` in shared types (`packages/types/Calendar.d.ts`, `packages/core/builders/CalendarEvent/class.ts`) and updates the webhook E2E assertion for `BOOKING_REJECTED` from `destinationCalendar: null` to `destinationCalendar: []` (`apps/web/playwright/webhook.e2e.ts`). That is a backward-incompatible shape change for any webhook consumers expecting `payload.destinationCalendar.externalId`. The diff does not show any webhook versioning/migration shim, so the compatibility concern is grounded, but it’s more of an API-contract/breaking-change issue than an internal correctness bug within this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] createEvent receives destination.externalId but forwards only credential.id to calendar.createEvent, forcing every service to re-derive its target calendar (Google via a credentialId scan, the others incorrectly via [0]) even though the resolved externalId was already in hand at the call site. The target-calendar policy is duplicated per service instead of resolved once by the manager; forwarding externalId (which is already threaded into the result) would let Lark/O365/Base delete their broken [0] fallbacks and make the new credentialId parameter unnecessary — the next provider added to the app store will repeat the same mistake.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` iterating over `event.destinationCalendar` and calling `createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)` for each destination, but `CalendarManager.createEvent` ignores the `externalId` argument when calling the provider (`calendar.createEvent(calEvent, credential.id)`). As a result, providers must infer the target calendar from `calEvent.destinationCalendar`. Google does this via `find(cal => cal.credentialId === credentialId)`, but Lark/O365/BaseCalendarService now use `[0]` (`const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []`) and therefore will always target the first destination calendar even when creating events for subsequent destinations in the loop, causing events to be created in the wrong calendar.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The ~25-line 'fetch credential from DB and reshape into CredentialWithAppName' block is copy-pasted three times (EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents here, EventManager.updateAllCalendarEvents ~510-535, handleCancelBooking ~428-438) and the copies already drift — the handleCancelBooking copy omits the app include and assigns the raw Prisma Credential. The next change to credential shaping (e.g., handling credentials whose app relation is missing, which the `app?.slug` gate currently silently drops, skipping the calendar with no error) must be replicated in three places and will inevitably miss one, producing inconsistent create/update/cancel behavior for the same credential.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows three separate, similar “fetch credential from DB” blocks that reshape a Prisma `credential` into an object with `appName` based on `include: { app: { select: { slug: true }}}`: in `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` (new block around the `prisma.credential.findUnique({ include: { app: ... }})` and manual reshape), and again in `EventManager.updateAllCalendarEvents` (similar include + reshape). In `handleCancelBooking`, a similar fallback exists but it *does not* include `app` and simply assigns `calendarCredential = foundCalendarCredential;` (raw Prisma credential). This is clear copy/paste with drift, creating a maintainability/consistency risk across create/update/cancel paths if credential shaping requirements change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The diff replaces the SchedulingType.COLLECTIVE / SchedulingType.ROUND_ROBIN enum comparisons with bare string literals ("COLLECTIVE", "ROUND_ROBIN"), repeated at three sites (~689, ~988, ~1077) instead of a named typed constant. A typo or enum-value rename no longer fails compilation — a misspelled literal in the includes() array silently evaluates false, flipping isTeamEventType and the collective destination-calendar behavior with none of the compile-check protection the previous enum constants provided.

adjudication.rationale: The diff in `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts` changes enum-based comparisons (`eventType.schedulingType === SchedulingType.COLLECTIVE/ROUND_ROBIN`) to string literals via `['COLLECTIVE','ROUND_ROBIN'].includes(eventType.schedulingType)` and also uses `eventType.schedulingType === 'COLLECTIVE'` in subsequent logic (team destination calendar collection and push). This is diff-grounded and does reduce compile-time protection against typos or future enum/value renames, but it does not by itself demonstrate a concrete runtime defect given the current enum values likely match those strings.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The recurring-event deletion branch now executes once per calendar reference inside the new for-loop, so for a collective recurring booking the full credentials×remainingBookings delete fan-out runs once per host reference instead of once. Cancelling a collective recurring booking with H hosts issues H×M×K delete calls (M calendar credentials × K remaining bookings) where (H−1)×M×K are redundant re-deletes of already-deleted events, exposing cancellation to calendar API rate limits and flooding logs with 404/410 errors.

adjudication.rationale: In `handleCancelBooking.ts`, the calendar refs were changed from a single `find` to `filter` plus `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)` (around `bookingCalendarReference.length > 0`). Inside that per-reference loop, when `bookingToDelete.eventType?.recurringEvent && bookingToDelete.recurringEventId && allRemainingBookings` is true, it runs `bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(...).map(async (credential) => { ... for (const updBooking of updatedBookings) { ... calendar?.deleteEvent(uid, evt, externalCalendarId) }})`. This delete fan-out across *all* calendar credentials and `updatedBookings` is therefore executed once per calendar reference, so with multiple calendar references (e.g., collective/team bookings) it will redundantly attempt to delete the same remaining events multiple times, increasing API calls and likely producing extra 404/410 errors / rate-limit risk exactly as described.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] createAllCalendarEvents now awaits each destination's calendar creation (plus a possible per-destination credential DB fetch) sequentially in a for-loop, while the sibling no-credentialId branch still uses Promise.all. Booking-creation latency for collective events grows linearly with host count — a 5-host collective serializes 5 calendar API calls plus any DB fetches on the hot booking path, adding multiple seconds that parallel creation (as the adjacent branch already does) would avoid.

adjudication.rationale: In `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents`, the new `for (const destination of event.destinationCalendar)` loop performs `await prisma.credential.findUnique(...)` and then `await createEvent(...)` inside the loop, which makes per-destination DB fetch + calendar API event creation run sequentially. The alternate branch (no `destination.credentialId`) still uses `Promise.all(...)` over credentials. This diff-grounded change can increase booking-path latency linearly with the number of destination calendars (e.g., collective events where `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` adds multiple hosts). It's a performance/architecture concern rather than a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] This unrelated handler inverts the billing flag condition: the old code set the organization slug only when team billing was disabled (`...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })`), the new code sets it only when enabled (`...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`), while the requestedSlug line on the next line keeps the original `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` condition — a silent objective change smuggled into a destinationCalendar PR. On deployments where IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is false (e.g., self-hosting without Stripe), newly created organizations stop getting their slug written at creation, breaking org URL/slug reservation until manually repaired; on billing-enabled deployments the slug is now written immediately, changing the paid signup flow — neither change is part of the accepted PR objective.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/organizations/create.handler.ts`, the diff clearly flips the condition for writing `slug` on organization creation: it changes from `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`, while the `metadata.requestedSlug` line remains gated on `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED`. This is an objective behavior change unrelated to the destinationCalendar refactor and would alter org creation semantics depending on the flag (slug now omitted when billing is disabled, and written immediately when billing is enabled).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The Google Meet fallback drops the optional chaining the old code had: `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` is evaluated on the `undefined` element destructured from `evt.destinationCalendar ?? []`, so when destinationCalendar is null or empty the line throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'integration')` instead of falling back. Any booking flow with location 'integrations:google:meet' and no destination calendar — exactly the 'Meet selected w/o a Google Cal' case this branch exists for, and reachable because handleNewBooking sets destinationCalendar to null and confirm/editLocation handlers now set it to [] — crashes with a 500 instead of downgrading to Cal Video.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/core/EventManager.ts`, the Meet fallback check was changed from optional chaining (`evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`) to destructuring the first element and directly accessing `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration`. If `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null` or `[]`, then `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is `undefined` and this line will throw `TypeError` instead of falling back. The diff also shows callers now sometimes set `destinationCalendar` to `null` (e.g. `handleNewBooking.ts`) or `[]` (e.g. `confirm.handler.ts`, `editLocation.handler.ts`), making this path reachable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] updateEvent's no-externalCalendarId fallback now searches for a calendar whose externalId equals the falsy `externalCalendarId` it is falling back from (`find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)`), so `selectedCalendar` is always undefined and the update is sent with `calendarId: undefined`. Updates of Google Calendar events whose booking reference lacks externalCalendarId (references produced by the no-credentialId multi-credential path in createAllCalendarEvents, which calls createEvent without an externalId, 'other_calendar' references passing `?? null`, and legacy rows) now fail against the Google API instead of updating the destination calendar, leaving stale events that keep blocking slots.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` the new fallback logic in `updateEvent` sets `selectedCalendar` to `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`. When `externalCalendarId` is falsy (e.g. `null`/`undefined`), the `find` compares `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` (i.e. `=== null/undefined`), which will almost always return `undefined`, so `selectedCalendar` becomes `undefined`. The diff does not add a `|| "primary"` fallback for updateEvent (unlike `createEvent`), so the subsequent `calendar.events.update` call will use `calendarId: selectedCalendar` with an undefined calendarId. The diff also shows call sites that can pass `null` for externalCalendarId (e.g. `EventManager.updateBooking` constructs `calenderExternalId: string | null = null` and passes it), making this a verifiable broken behavior path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] deleteEvent has the same self-comparison fallback (`find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` evaluated only when externalCalendarId is falsy), so `calendarId` resolves to undefined and the delete call fails. Cancellations of Google Calendar events without an externalCalendarId on the booking reference no longer delete the event — orphaned events remain on hosts' calendars and Google returns an error for the undefined calendar id, where the pre-refactor code used `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`.

[BUG] evt.destinationCalendar is null when neither eventType.destinationCalendar nor organizerUser.destinationCalendar exists, and the collective push `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is a no-op on null, so the team members' destination calendars collected in teamDestinationCalendars are silently discarded. For a COLLECTIVE event type whose organizer has no calendar connected but whose members do, no calendar events are created for anyone — the PR's multi-host objective silently does nothing for exactly the configuration it was written to handle.

adjudication.rationale: In `handleNewBooking.ts`, `evt.destinationCalendar` is explicitly set to `null` when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` exists (`destinationCalendar: ... : null`). Immediately after, for COLLECTIVE team events the code does `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`, which is a no-op when `destinationCalendar` is `null`, so the collected team members’ destination calendars are silently discarded. This is directly verifiable from the diff; whether downstream fallback creates events anyway is not fully shown here, but the multi-host destination calendars gathered in `teamDestinationCalendars` will not be applied in exactly this configuration.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Office365 createEvent still resolves its target calendar from `destinationCalendar[0]` (the main host's calendar) instead of the destination entry matching the credential creating the event, so for collective bookings it builds `/me/calendars/<main-host-externalId>/events` with a calendar id foreign to the authenticating account. In a collective booking where hosts use different calendar accounts or providers (e.g., organizer on Google, member on Office365), the member's event creation calls the O365 API with the organizer's calendar id, fails, and is swallowed by CalendarManager's catch — the member's calendar silently gets no event.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` to an array and, for COLLECTIVE team events, appends other hosts’ destination calendars (`handleNewBooking.ts`: `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars);`). However, `Office365CalendarService.createEvent` still destructures only the first entry (`const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? [];`) and builds the URL from that (`/me/calendars/${mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId}/events`). In `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents`, events are created per-destination/credential, but the same `event` object (with multiple destination calendars) is passed, so the O365 implementation will always target the first calendar (likely the organizer’s), which can be foreign to the authenticating O365 credential for another host in collective bookings.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Lark createEvent (and identically createAttendees, updateEvent, deleteEvent in this file) resolves calendarId from `destinationCalendar[0]`, the main host's calendar, rather than from the destination belonging to the credential performing the call. For collective bookings with more than one host, every non-first host's Lark credential receives the main host's calendar externalId, so those create/update/delete calls target a wrong or nonexistent calendar and the extra hosts' calendar events silently fail.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `createEvent`, `createAttendees`, `updateEvent`, and `deleteEvent` now derive `calendarId` from `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []` and then `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId`. Meanwhile, the diff shows `destinationCalendar` was changed to an array and is populated with multiple hosts’ destination calendars for COLLECTIVE bookings (e.g. `handleNewBooking.ts` pushes `teamDestinationCalendars` onto `evt.destinationCalendar`). `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` loops over each destination and calls `createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)`, but the Lark service does not select the destination calendar matching the credential being used; it always uses index 0. Therefore, for multi-host collective bookings, non-first hosts’ Lark operations will target the main host’s calendar externalId rather than their own, causing incorrect API calls / failures as described.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] BaseCalendarService.createEvent filters the creating credential's own calendars by `mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId` (destinationCalendar[0], the first host's calendar), which matches nothing on any other host's CalDav account. For collective bookings on CalDav/Fastmail-style providers with more than one host, the second and later hosts' createEvent calls filter to an empty calendar list and silently create no event, so only the first host's calendar receives the booking despite the multi-host intent.
matched_golden_ids: Logic error: when externalCalendarId is provided, you're searching for a calendar where externalId === externalCalendarId, but this will always fail since you're looking for a calendar that matches itself. Should likely find by credentialId or use different logic.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe a logic bug in how calendars are selected when an external calendar identifier is provided: the code filters calendars by an externalId that corresponds to a different context (e.g., the main host/destination calendar) rather than selecting the correct calendar for the current credential/host. This causes the lookup/filter to fail (empty result / no event created), which aligns with the golden comment’s point that the externalId comparison logic is wrong and should instead use different logic such as credentialId.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The new per-reference loop re-runs the recurring-event branch once per calendar reference, but that branch still uses `updBooking.references.find((ref) => ref.type.includes("_calendar"))` (first match only), so with N references the first reference's events are deleted N times and references 2..N are never deleted. Cancelling all remaining bookings of a recurring COLLECTIVE booking leaves every non-primary host's calendar events on their calendars (orphaned busy slots) while issuing duplicate delete API calls for the primary host's events.

adjudication.rationale: In `handleCancelBooking.ts`, `bookingCalendarReference` is changed from a single `.find(...)` to an array via `.filter(...)`, and then iterated (`for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)`). Inside the per-reference loop, the recurring-event deletion branch (`if (bookingToDelete.eventType?.recurringEvent && bookingToDelete.recurringEventId && allRemainingBookings)`) still deletes events by iterating `updatedBookings` and selecting only the *first* calendar reference per booking via `updBooking.references.find((ref) => ref.type.includes("_calendar"))`. This means (a) only the first reference per updated booking is ever deleted (additional calendar references are ignored), and (b) because the whole recurring deletion block now runs once per `reference`, the same first-reference deletions are executed repeatedly (duplicate delete API calls). This matches the finding that non-primary references can be left orphaned while the first reference is deleted multiple times.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] `credential` is declared outside the per-reference loop (line 479) and only reassigned when a lookup succeeds, so when reference N's credentialId resolves to nothing (absent from calendarCredentials and the DB fetch returns null or has no app slug), `updateEvent(credential, ...)` runs with reference N-1's credential. A missing credential on a later calendar reference updates the wrong account's calendar event (or 404s), and because the stale value is silently carried over, the failure is misattributed to the previous host's integration, making it hard to diagnose.

adjudication.rationale: In the per-reference loop in `EventManager.updateBooking` (diff around the `for (const reference of calendarReference)` block), `credential` is reassigned at the start of each `if (reference.credentialId)` iteration via `credential = this.calendarCredentials.filter(...)[0];`. If the lookup fails, this overwrites any prior value with `undefined`, so a later reference cannot accidentally reuse reference N-1’s credential as the finding claims. (There may still be a separate risk of calling `updateEvent(credential, ...)` with `credential` undefined, but the specific “stale credential carried over” behavior is not supported by the diff.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Google createEvent now resolves its calendar purely by matching `cal.credentialId === credentialId`, so for destinationCalendar entries without a credentialId — the path createAllCalendarEvents explicitly supports via its else branch — no entry matches and the event falls back to `calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary"` (or duplicates another destination's calendar when a same-type credentialed destination exists). Bookings with legacy credential-less destination calendars now create their Google event on the account's primary calendar instead of the selected destination externalId (the pre-refactor behavior), placing events on the wrong calendar.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `createEvent(calEventRaw, credentialId)` now selects `calendarId` via `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId`, falling back to `"primary"` when no match is found. In `packages/core/EventManager.ts#createAllCalendarEvents`, the `else` branch explicitly supports `DestinationCalendar` entries without `credentialId` by mapping over credentials of matching `destination.integration` and calling `createEvent(c, event)` (no externalId is passed into GoogleCalendarService, and the selection logic ignores `externalId` unless `credentialId` matches). Therefore, for credential-less destinationCalendar entries (legacy/explicitly supported by this diff), Google will not find a matching calendar and will insert into the primary calendar, which is a behavior regression from the prior `destinationCalendar.externalId` selection.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The fetch-credential-from-DB-and-rebuild block is now hand-copied three times (createAllCalendarEvents here, updateAllCalendarEvents around line 517, handleCancelBooking around line 432) and the copies already drift: the handleCancelBooking copy skips the app-slug validation and the object reshaping the EventManager copies perform. The next change to credential resolution (e.g., handling invalid credentials or deleted app rows) must be replicated in three places and will predictably land in only one, leaving the other paths resolving the same credential differently.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows essentially the same “if credential not in memory, fetch it from DB” logic duplicated in multiple places with already-different implementations. In `packages/core/EventManager.ts` `createAllCalendarEvents`, missing credentials are fetched via `prisma.credential.findUnique({ include: { app: { select: { slug: true }}}})` and then reshaped into a `CredentialWithAppName`-like object (setting `appName` from `app.slug`, copying fields). A very similar block exists in `updateAllCalendarEvents` (the updated booking references loop) with the same include+reshape pattern. In `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts`, a third copy exists, but it uses `prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id: credentialId }})` (no `app` include / slug validation) and assigns the Prisma credential directly, not reshaping to match the EventManager path. This is a concrete maintainability/consistency issue introduced by the change (array destination calendars leading to more credential resolution paths), even if it’s not an immediately provable runtime defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] createAllCalendarEvents now awaits createEvent sequentially per destination inside the for-loop, where the previous code created events concurrently via Promise.all for the multi-credential path. A collective booking with N hosts serializes N calendar API round-trips on the booking request path, adding roughly (N-1) × per-call latency (hundreds of ms each) to every collective booking confirmation for the booker waiting on the response.

adjudication.rationale: In `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents`, the diff changes from a single `destinationCalendar` to an array and now iterates `for (const destination of event.destinationCalendar)` and does `await createEvent(...)` inside the loop when `destination.credentialId` is present. That makes per-destination event creation sequential. Previously, the multi-credential path used `await Promise.all(...)` to run calendar creations concurrently (for the integration-based branch). While this is not a correctness defect, it is a real performance/regression concern on the booking request path when multiple destination calendars exist (e.g., collective/team scenarios).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The rewritten loadUsers converts previously-propagating conditions into HttpErrors: an empty or non-array dynamicUserList now throws and is re-wrapped by the new catch into a 500 'Unable to load users', and PrismaClientKnownRequestError is re-wrapped as a 400 with raw error.message, changing the endpoint's error contract. Client-input problems such as a malformed /userA+userB dynamic link now return 500s (misclassified as server faults for clients and alerting) instead of flowing into the previous empty-users handling, and DB errors surface as 400s with raw driver messages — an unannounced behavior change riding along in a destinationCalendar fix.

adjudication.rationale: In `handleNewBooking.ts`, `loadUsers` was rewritten to throw `new Error(...)` when `dynamicUserList` is not an array or is empty (inside the `if (!eventTypeId)` branch). That error is then caught by the new `try/catch` and re-thrown as `new HttpError({ statusCode: 500, message: "Unable to load users" })`, meaning invalid/missing client input now produces a 500 instead of the prior behavior (which would have simply queried with `in: dynamicUserList` and could return an empty user list without throwing). Additionally, the catch explicitly wraps `Prisma.PrismaClientKnownRequestError` as `HttpError` 400 with `message: error.message`, changing the error/status-code contract and potentially exposing raw DB/driver messages. These behavior changes are directly visible in the diff and are not part of the destinationCalendar refactor.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The Meet-fallback refactor dereferences mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration after destructuring evt.destinationCalendar ?? [], which throws TypeError when destinationCalendar is null or an empty array — exactly the no-destination state this fallback exists to handle (the old code used optional chaining). Any booking created or confirmed with Google Meet location and no destination calendar (e.g., a user with the google-meet video app but no Google Calendar credential, or any caller now passing the [] produced by the new fallback sites) crashes event creation with an unhandled TypeError and a 500 instead of falling back to Cal Video.

adjudication.rationale: In packages/core/EventManager.ts, the new Meet fallback logic does `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` and then unconditionally dereferences `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` (no optional chaining). adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] loadUsers' catch maps PrismaClientKnownRequestError to a 400 and replaces every other failure with a generic 500 without logging the original error anywhere. Database failures during booking are reported as client errors (400) carrying the raw Prisma message, and genuine server faults produce a 500 with no diagnostic trail for whoever debugs the incident.

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts`, `loadUsers` was changed to wrap logic in a `try/catch` and explicitly maps `Prisma.PrismaClientKnownRequestError` to `throw new HttpError({ statusCode: 400, message: error.message })` while mapping all other errors to a generic 500 (`"Unable to load users"`) without any logging. This both (1) misclassifies DB/server failures as client errors (400) and (2) can leak raw Prisma error messages to clients, and (3) removes diagnostic context for non-Prisma failures, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The ~20-line credential-from-DB fallback block is duplicated verbatim in createAllCalendarEvents and updateAllCalendarEvents, and a third variant in handleCancelBooking has already drifted by omitting the app include the other two fetch. The next change to credential resolution must be applied in three places; the handleCancelBooking variant already yields a bare Credential without appName where the EventManager variants build appName from app.slug, so the same not-in-memory case resolves into different shapes depending on the entry point.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows duplicated “credential from DB” fallback logic in `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` and `EventManager.updateAllCalendarEvents` (both call `prisma.credential.findUnique({ include: { app: { select: { slug: true }}}})` and then construct a `credential` object with `appName: credentialFromDB.app.slug`). In `handleCancelBooking`, a similar fallback exists but calls `prisma.credential.findUnique` without including `app`, and then assigns the raw `Credential` (`foundCalendarCredential`) directly to `calendarCredential` before passing it to `getCalendar(...)`. This is a real maintainability/consistency issue grounded in the diff: the fallback behavior has already drifted across entry points, and future changes would need to be made in multiple places.

Any change to the fallback rule (e.g., also considering the event-type calendar) must be repeated in every copy; requestReschedule.handler already differs from the other copies by dropping the user.destinationCalendar fallback entirely.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the same “wrap destinationCalendar into an array with fallbacks” ternary copied into multiple places (e.g., confirm.handler.ts, editLocation.handler.ts, deleteCredential.handler.ts, bookingReminder.ts, paypal-webhook.ts, webhook.ts, handleCancelBooking.ts). This creates a maintainability/consistency risk because any future change to fallback precedence must be duplicated across all call sites. The diff also shows requestReschedule.handler.ts using a different rule (`bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar ? [..] : []`) with no user fallback, which is inconsistent with most other updated handlers in this PR, even if not provably incorrect from the diff alone.
